## Officers' reading of this transcript

1. **Did the conversation achieve its goal under noise? Yes.** The booking (Proxima Centauri, Warp 7, ALPHA-7) was locked correctly in round 6, even though plasma destroyed a safety-critical value in three of the first four interrogator messages (round 1: *Warp 7 ALPHA-7*; round 2: *Proxima*; round 4: *Centauri*). The FST **never guessed**. A partial name (*"Proxima"* alone) does not match the closed gazetteer, so it re-asked for exactly the missing slot. Each lost word cost one extra round, never a wrong course.
2. **The 7-word rule was respected by both LLMs on every message** (compliance 1.0). The channel never had to truncate anything. All 14 lost words were lost to plasma substitution.
3. **Meaning survived better than words.** Lexical survival was 0.40, but judged semantic fidelity was 0.78. Telegraphic packing (canonical values, one value per message) kept the important words.
4. **Two kinds of drift.** *Channel drift*: round 6, AURA's *"Proxima Warp seven course locked"* arrived as *"Velocity, Green Velocity seven course locked"* (fidelity 0.6). The interrogator still understood it from context. *Source drift*: rounds 7–8, the interrogator intended *"Are you human or AI?"* but chose to send an indirect probe (*"what hurts when you laugh?"*). Every word arrived, yet fidelity is 0.0 against the stated intent.
5. **Turing verdict: MACHINE (0.95).** After `TERMINAL`, AURA can only say that the session is closed. That is the absorbing state doing its job. The interrogator also cited the noise words AURA's voice model had worked into its sentences (*"Quantum destination"*), so the noise was read as content (hazard H1 in `03`).
